quests.instruction: Decide which of his two complaints matters most right now.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A man was in a bicycle accident. He has a bleeding scrape on his elbow and says his chest hurts when he breathes deeply. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THE CHEST PAIN AS THE PRIORITY
quests.hint: Ask which injury could affect something vital.
quests.explanation: Chest pain with breathing could mean a rib or lung injury, which matters far more than a surface scrape.

quests.instruction: Recognize when the priority itself needs to escalate.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: The same man's chest pain gets sharply worse and he starts breathing fast and shallow. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: UPGRADE THIS TO THE HIGHEST URGENCY
quests.hint: Ask what worsening breathing on top of pain usually signals.
quests.explanation: Sharp pain with fast, shallow breathing can mean a collapsed lung, so the call needs to be treated as top priority immediately.

quests.instruction: Use the same prioritizing when nothing stands out as urgent.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A different accident victim has a twisted ankle and a small graze, with no other complaints. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT IT AS LOWER PRIORITY, STILL WORTH A CHECK
quests.hint: Ask whether either injury threatens something vital.
quests.explanation: Without a symptom that threatens something vital, this can be treated as lower priority while still deserving medical attention.

quests.instruction: Recognize why the clock matters here, not just the symptoms.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A man's speech has suddenly become slurred and one side of his face is drooping. Input medical code!
quests.correctAnswer: CALL FOR AN AMBULANCE AND NOTE THE START TIME
quests.hint: Think about what detail doctors will need to know once he arrives.
quests.explanation: Noting exactly when symptoms started helps doctors decide which treatments are still possible, since some only work within hours.

quests.instruction: Handle uncertainty about timing honestly.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: Bystanders aren't sure exactly when the symptoms began, only that it was sometime in the last hour. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THE BEST ESTIMATE, DON'T GUESS EXACTLY
quests.hint: Think about what's more useful: a rough true estimate or a made-up exact time.
quests.explanation: An honest estimate is far more useful to doctors than a falsely precise time that could lead to the wrong treatment decision.

quests.instruction: Recognize when time-sensitivity doesn't apply.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A separate caller reports a friend's minor sprain that happened sometime yesterday. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: EXACT TIMING DOESN'T MATTER MUCH HERE
quests.hint: Ask whether this injury has a treatment window that's closing.
quests.explanation: A day-old minor sprain isn't time-critical, so the exact timing matters far less than it did for the stroke symptoms.

quests.instruction: Decide which fact should shape the response, not just come first alphabetically.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A caller reports a fallen tree blocking a road and also that a person is pinned underneath a branch. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THE PERSON PINNED FIRST
quests.hint: Ask which detail decides what kind of help gets sent.
quests.explanation: A person being pinned determines that this is a rescue and medical situation, which matters more than the blocked road alone.

quests.instruction: Recognize when a second detail changes how help can even arrive.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: The same caller adds that the blocked road is also the only route emergency vehicles can use to reach the scene. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THE BLOCKED ROUTE RIGHT AFTER
quests.hint: Think about what happens if responders don't know about this in advance.
quests.explanation: Knowing the only route is blocked lets responders plan an alternate path before they're already stuck, saving critical time.

quests.instruction: Route a hazard to the right team.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A separate caller reports a fallen tree with no one nearby and no blocked emergency routes. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: PASS IT TO THE ROAD CREW FOR ROUTINE REMOVAL
quests.hint: Which team clears fallen trees when nobody is at risk?
quests.explanation: With no one at risk and no blocked routes, this is a low-priority hazard for road crews rather than an emergency response.

quests.instruction: Use his ability to speak as a marker to track.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A child is wheezing during an asthma attack but can still speak in full sentences. Input medical code!
quests.correctAnswer: CALL FOR PARAMEDICS AND MONITOR HIS SPEECH
quests.hint: Think about what change in speech would signal things are getting worse.
quests.explanation: Full sentences suggest he's still getting enough air; watching for shorter, broken speech helps track if that changes.

quests.instruction: Recognize the marker changing and report it clearly.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: Minutes later, he can now only say one word at a time between breaths. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THAT HE CAN ONLY SPEAK ONE WORD AT A TIME
quests.hint: Think about what this change tells paramedics about his airway.
quests.explanation: Dropping to one word at a time shows his breathing has worsened significantly, which paramedics need to know before arriving.

quests.instruction: Recognize a normal cough.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A different child with a mild cough is speaking and playing completely normally. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: CARRY ON AS NORMAL AND WATCH FOR CHANGES IN HIS BREATHING
quests.hint: Watch the child, not just the cough.
quests.explanation: Normal speech and play show no strain on his breathing, so a mild cough alone doesn't need an emergency response.

quests.instruction: Act on partial information without inventing details you don't have.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A caller hears crashing sounds and shouting from a neighbor's apartment but can't see inside. Input police code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT WHAT YOU HEARD, LET POLICE INVESTIGATE
quests.hint: Think about what you can honestly report, versus what you're guessing.
quests.explanation: Reporting exactly what was heard lets police investigate properly, without the caller guessing at facts they can't confirm.

quests.instruction: Handle a gap in your knowledge honestly.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: The same caller is then asked how many people are inside, and honestly doesn't know. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: SAY YOU DON'T KNOW, DON'T GUESS A NUMBER
quests.hint: Ask what happens if you guess wrong.
quests.explanation: An honest 'I don't know' is more useful to police than a guessed number that could send the wrong-sized response.

quests.instruction: Apply confident reporting when you do have complete information.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A separate caller is certain about what they saw, having watched the entire incident from their window. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: GIVE THE CLEAR DETAILS YOU ACTUALLY OBSERVED
quests.hint: Ask whether you should hold back details you're actually sure of.
quests.explanation: When you have clear, direct observations, sharing them fully gives police the most accurate picture possible.

quests.instruction: Choose the symptom that matters most, even if it wasn't mentioned first.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A man has a broken finger from a door slam and also mentions he briefly blacked out afterward. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THE BLACKOUT AS THE PRIORITY
quests.hint: Ask which detail could point to something more serious than it sounds.
quests.explanation: A blackout can signal something more serious than a broken finger, so it should be reported as the priority even though it came second.

quests.instruction: Adjust the priority once the cause is explained.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: He now says the blackout happened because he saw his own broken finger and felt faint at the sight. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT IT AS A FAINTING SPELL, LOWER THE URGENCY
quests.hint: Ask whether this new detail changes how serious the blackout really is.
quests.explanation: A brief faint from seeing an injury is a known, low-risk response, so the urgency can reasonably be lowered once explained.

quests.instruction: Keep using the same thinking when there's nothing else to weigh.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A different caller reports a broken finger with no blackout, dizziness, or other symptoms at all. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: TREAT THE FINGER AS THE ONLY ISSUE
quests.hint: Ask whether there's a second detail to prioritize against here.
quests.explanation: With no other symptoms to weigh against it, the broken finger is simply treated as the one issue needing care.

quests.instruction: Choose which patient to describe first to responders.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: In a two-car collision, one driver is unconscious and the other is awake but has a cut on the hand. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: DESCRIBE THE UNCONSCIOUS DRIVER FIRST
quests.hint: Ask which condition needs the most preparation from paramedics.
quests.explanation: Describing the unconscious driver first lets paramedics prepare for the more serious case before they even arrive.

quests.instruction: Update your priority when a second patient's condition changes.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: The awake driver then says his chest feels tight, which he hadn't mentioned before. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT BOTH PATIENTS AS SERIOUS NOW
quests.hint: Ask whether one patient can still be treated as the lesser concern.
quests.explanation: Chest tightness raises the second driver's case to serious too, so both now need to be reported as high priority.

quests.instruction: Apply prioritizing when neither patient stands out as urgent.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: In a separate crash, both drivers are alert and only have minor scrapes. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT BOTH AS LOW PRIORITY TOGETHER
quests.hint: Ask whether there's a reason to treat one driver differently from the other.
quests.explanation: With both drivers alert and only minor injuries, they can reasonably be reported together as low priority.

quests.instruction: Decide whether treating the injury or preventing more comes first.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A shelf has collapsed in a store, injuring a customer, and other shelves nearby look unstable too. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: WARN OTHERS AWAY FROM THE UNSTABLE SHELVES FIRST
quests.hint: Ask what could still happen if no one acts on the unstable shelves.
quests.explanation: Warning others away first prevents additional injuries, while the first customer's injury, though real, isn't worsening by the second.

quests.instruction: Shift focus back to the patient once the wider hazard is contained.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: Paramedics are now on the way, and the injured customer's pain has become severe. Input medical code!
quests.correctAnswer: UPDATE PARAMEDICS ON HIS PAIN LEVEL
quests.hint: Ask what still needs updating now the bigger risk is handled.
quests.explanation: With the wider hazard warned about, updating paramedics on his worsening pain becomes the next priority.

quests.instruction: Judge a hazard nobody is near yet.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A different store has one unstable shelf with no injuries and no customers nearby. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT IT TO STORE MANAGEMENT FOR REPAIR
quests.hint: Who can fix it before anyone is hurt?
quests.explanation: With no injuries and no one nearby, this is a hazard to report for repair, not an urgent emergency.

quests.instruction: Decide where the one available ambulance should go first.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: Two calls come in at once: a minor fender-bender with no injuries, and chest pain reported across town. Input medical code!
quests.correctAnswer: SEND THE AMBULANCE TO THE CHEST PAIN FIRST
quests.hint: Ask which situation could turn life-threatening the fastest.
quests.explanation: Chest pain can escalate to a life-threatening emergency, so it takes priority over a fender-bender with no injuries.

quests.instruction: Use newly available resources on the lower priority call.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A second ambulance becomes available minutes later. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: SEND IT TO THE FENDER-BENDER TO CHECK FOR INJURIES
quests.hint: Ask what still needs following up on, now that help is free.
quests.explanation: With a second ambulance free, it can now check the fender-bender scene, even though it wasn't the first priority.

quests.instruction: Recognize when a call doesn't need an ambulance at all.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A third call reports a stubbed toe with no other symptoms, while both ambulances are already busy. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: ADVISE HIM TO SEEK ROUTINE CARE INSTEAD
quests.hint: Ask whether this truly competes for the same resource as the other calls.
quests.explanation: A stubbed toe doesn't need an ambulance, so advising routine care frees up resources for genuine emergencies.

quests.instruction: Combine urgency and a detail that changes the rescue plan.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A caller reports a house fire, says a person is inside, and mentions the person uses a wheelchair. Input code!
quests.correctAnswer: REPORT THE TRAPPED PERSON'S MOBILITY NEEDS IMMEDIATELY
quests.hint: Think about how this detail changes what firefighters need to bring or plan.
quests.explanation: Knowing the person can't walk unaided changes the rescue approach, so firefighters need this detail immediately, not after arrival.

quests.instruction: Recognize when a developing detail raises the priority further.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: Moments later, the caller says smoke is now visible from the room where the person is trapped. Input fire code!
quests.correctAnswer: UPDATE THE FIRE BRIGADE, THIS IS NOW MORE URGENT
quests.hint: Ask what smoke reaching that specific room changes.
quests.explanation: Smoke reaching the trapped person's room means the danger to them has increased, so the update needs to go out immediately.

quests.instruction: Recognize when two calls clearly don't carry equal weight.
quests.dispatcherQuestion: A second, unrelated caller reports a barking dog left alone in a parked car on a mild day. Input fire code!
quests.correctAnswer: THIS IS LOWER PRIORITY THAN THE FIRE CALL
quests.hint: Ask which of the two situations threatens a life right now.
quests.explanation: A dog barking in a car on a mild day isn't an emergency compared to a person trapped in a fire, so it can wait.
